reading.body:
The directory is a catalog structure, not a dataset: it promises a tool count across 23 categories and 63 in-depth profiles, but the total field is zero.

What the record actually establishes is the shape of the coverage. Tools are grouped into 23 categories, and 63 of them get full profiles covering pricing, strengths, weaknesses, and governance notes. The rest are listed without that depth. The distinction matters because pricing and governance notes are the fields that let a buyer compare products on cost and on constraints, not just on capability.

For AI specifically, this is a market-layer artifact. It describes how AI products are sold and documented, not what compute they run on or where that compute sits. Nothing here ties any tool to a building, a power contract, or a grid constraint, so the data cannot support a claim about the physical layer of AI at all.

The record also does not tell the reader which tools are covered, how the 23 categories are defined, or when the counts were last true. The total of zero against a described catalog of many tools is an unresolved inconsistency in the data itself, and it should be read as a gap rather than as evidence that no tools exist.
